title: HelixGen - Inference scaling, burst & streaming discovery
summary: Discovery with HelixGen about serving genomics assistant. Primary goals: p95 < 450ms for short-turn responses & sustained streaming at >= 120 tokens/sec for clinical drafts. Evaluating hosted for quick tests, dedicated for predictable bursts, private for data residency. Actionables: benchmark template, infra diagram, trial Dedicated pricing. Some mis-heard terms in transcript.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-02
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom (rec)
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marc (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood solutions), Sofia (CTO HelixGen), Evan (Staff ML Eng), Priya (Platform), Liam (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed p95 targets and burst patterns; difference between hosted/dedicated/private; network egress and VPC questions; agreed to run streaming token/sec benchmark and share infra diagrams; Redwood to provide pricing ranges for Dedicated reserve + burst.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, this is Aisha from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Sofia: Sofia here, hi.
[00:08] Evan: Evan on my end.
[00:09] Priya: Priya.
[00:11] Liam: Liam.
[00:12] Marc: Marc from the infra team.
[00:14] Aisha: Awesome. The goal today is to understand your latency and throughput needs, burst profile, and get the info we need for a Dedicated trial or private install. Maybe start with a quick description of the workload?
[00:28] Sofia: Sure, so HelixGen is building an assistant that drafts clinical notes and annotates sequencing logs. Most calls are short—like 1 to 3 turn conversations, ~150-400 tokens per call, but we also have long draft jobs > 1k tokens for report generation. Primary concern is p95 latency for the short interactive flows, ideally under 450 milliseconds end-to-end. For streaming we want steady-state of about 120 tokens/sec per session, with spikes up to 500 tps for batch drafting during off-hours.
[00:54] Aisha: Okay p95 <450ms, 120 sustained streaming and bursts to 500—got it. Are those user-visible latencies or just server-to-server?
[01:02] Sofia: User-visible, yes. From user action to first token and overall time.
[01:06] Evan: Also the environment constraint: we need data residency in EU for PHI, so private is likely, but we want to see what Hosted or Dedicated tradeoffs look like first.
[01:16] Marc: A few follow-ups—what concurrency per model are we talking? single model or model switching?
[01:21] Priya: We'll have multi-tenant routing, so expect about 80 concurrent interactive sessions at peak, plus 20 long-running drafting jobs. Peak CPU/GPU load needs to account for burst windows.
[01:32] Marc: Got it. So roughly 100 concurrent sessions. That matters a lot for batching and our kernel selection.
[01:37] Jordan: Quick note, when you say 450ms p95, is that first token or full-text? We should clarify because it changes batching strategy.
[01:44] Sofia: First token, yes. Full text latency can be slower for the long reports.
[01:50] Aisha: Good. Marc, on the Redwood side, we typically optimize kernels and batching differently for first-token SLO vs throughput SLOs. For first-token p95 we bias for single-request routing with small micro-batches, lower queue-time. For throughput we enable continuous batching and prefix KV caching.
[02:05] Marc: Are you seeing better numbers with quantized 13B vs 7B FP16 for that first token tradeoff?
[02:11] Jordan: In our lab, 13B q4_0 gives similar first-token to 7B FP16 because the quantization reduces memory pressure; we do see some quality drop for hallucination-sensitive prompts, but it depends.
[02:22] Evan: Hmm okay. For clinical text we probably need careful evals. We care about quality at top of conversation.
[02:27] Aisha: Understood. Could you give us a day/week profile for requests—are bursts sudden or ramp?
[02:33] Priya: Mostly morning ramp 08:30-10:30EU where clinicians triage, then steady mid-day, then a heavy batch window midnight UTC when labs run batch summarizations. Bursts can be sudden when on-call rotations trigger notifications.
[02:47] Liam: And our infra is EKS in eu-west-1, we prefer VPC peering and private link to any hosted endpoints; for Dedicated we'd want dedicated VPC.
[02:58] Marc: Any regulatory certs we need to consider? SOC2 is a must, ISO if possible?
[03:03] Sofia: SOC 2 mandatory. Also audit logs and KMS with CMK access.
[03:08] Aisha: Redwood's Private option supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; Dedicated has SLA and can be provisioned in a VPC. We'll include our SOC2 attestation in the doc pack.
[03:16] Evan: Great. For the benchmarks, what artifacts do you need from our side?
[03:20] Marc: Sorry, Evan—Marc here. We'll need a sample prompt set, infra metrics (HPA events, pod spinup times), and request RT distribution.
[03:27] Evan: Yeah, we'll compile that.
[03:29] Aisha: We'll send a benchmark template. The plan would be: you run a lightweight streaming sample and we'll run the same on our Dedicated lab to compare tokens/sec and p95.
[03:38] Sophia: (laughs) Sofia, and please don't call me Sophia in the notes.
[03:41] Aisha: Noted, Sofia.
[03:43] Jordan: Quick dive—about streaming: we need to split between model-side generation tokens/sec and network-level throttles. Are you pushing via chunked HTTP streaming or websockets?
[03:53] Priya: Websockets for the interactive sessions. For batch drafting we use chunked uploads and then stream responses to an S3-backed draft store.
[04:02] Marc: Websockets are fine; we instrumented the KV cache to persist between sessions when the same user context is hit. That helps for first-token after a short idle.
[04:12] Evan: One wrinkle: our infra uses an internal auth proxy and we need mTLS to the inference endpoint when hosted. Is that possible?
[04:19] Aisha: Hosted supports TLS, but mTLS and private peering are on Dedicated/Private. We can broker a Private endpoint with customer-managed certs.
[04:27] Priya: For Dedicated, how do you handle autoscaling during a 10x burst? We need cold-start bounds.
[04:34] Marc: Redwood's Dedicated supports reserved pools plus burst capacity and configurable autoscale policies. There's a warm pool option to avoid cold starts; we'll show the numbers in the ROI doc.
[04:44] Liam: How long to spin up a new GPU node and warm model? 30s? 2 minutes?
[04:49] Jordan: depends on image and serialization. For our fast-path we pre-load model shards and use warm-workers; typical warm-up to first-token is ~12-25s for 13B quantized in our lab, 5-8s for 7B fp16. Cold start with no warm workers can be 90-180s.
[05:03] Sofia: That's significant. Do you offer pre-warming schedules tied to cron/batch windows?
[05:08] Aisha: Yes, you can schedule warm pools ahead of known bursts. We can also support predictive warmers tied to traffic signals.
[05:14] Evan: Ok good. About p95 measurement: do you measure client-to-first-token or your internal server timing?
[05:20] Marc: We capture both. In the console you can choose the SLO anchor: from ingress to first-token or e2e including network. We'll provide per-token CPU/GPU breakouts in the dashboard.
[05:30] Priya: For our security team we need proof that logs are immutable and retention policy configurable.
[05:35] Aisha: Private supports that. Dedicated also can forward to your SIEM with configurable retention.
[05:41] Jordan: Back to throughput—when you say 120 tokens/sec per session, is that sustained per user or aggregate per model?
[05:47] Sofia: Per session sustained for drafting flows. So multiply by concurrency for aggregate. If 80 sessions at 120 that's 9.6k tokens/sec aggregate. We'll probably cap the drafting jobs to avoid starving interactive sessions.
[05:58] Marc: Interesting, so we'd recommend prioritization: interactive sessions get low-latency lane, draft jobs in best-effort or queued lane. Redwood supports route-based policies.
[06:07] Evan: Any guidance on batching window sizes if we target <450ms p95 first token?
[06:12] Jordan: For that SLO, we keep batching windows ~5-10ms and microbatch sizes 1-4. Larger batching reduces cost but increases tail latency. There's a tunable trade-off.
[06:22] Aisha: We'll include suggested batching profiles in the recommendations.
[06:25] Sofia: Also, we have some long-running pipelines that stream 10k tokens—how do you handle KV cache memory and eviction?
[06:33] Marc: We have LRU policy per session; long streams are chunked and only key contexts are cached. We can tune sequence length and kv window.
[06:40] Liam: Network egress costs for hosted—do you have numbers? Our finance team will ask.
[06:44] Aisha: We'll include a cost model: tokens, network egress, reserved-pool pricing. Dedicated removes public egress charges if within VPC peering but there are interconnect costs.
[06:54] Evan: Could you run a brief scenario with numbers? Say 9.6k tokens/sec sustained for 30 minutes daily, what kind of Dedicated pool sizing would you suggest?
[07:03] Jordan: Off the cuff: depends on model selection. For 13B quantized, one A100-like equivalence can sustain ~600-800 tokens/sec for streaming outputs depending on sequence length. So for 9.6k you'd need ~12-16 equivalent units. We'll model this precisely in the spreadsheet.
[07:19] Priya: Are those numbers from the hosted lab or from customer-toned benchmarks?
[07:23] Jordan: Lab numbers with our continuous batching sim; we'll run the same workload in our Dedicated lab to approximate. Real customer payloads can vary +/-.
[07:33] Aisha: Next steps recap coming up—anything on compliance or procurement?
[07:37] Sofia: Procurement wants an initial commercial term for a 3-month Dedicated trial and pricing ballpark for reserved + burst.
[07:44] Aisha: We'll include a pilot pricing page and a reserved pool option in the follow-up email.
[07:49] Marc: One technical note—if you require private in EU we might need to schedule a quick architecture alignment call with our Private team and your security folks.
[07:58] Priya: Yes please.
[08:00] Aisha: Okay. We'll do that.
[08:03] (several minutes of side discussion about dates and availability omitted)
[10:15] Evan: Quick question—how do you handle model fallbacks under capacity pressure? Do you serve a lighter quantized variant or route to another region?
[10:23] Jordan: We have fallback policies—route to lower-cost model variant, spill to another region if latency acceptable, or serve cached completions. For PHI we default to non-cross-region unless allowed.
[10:34] Sofia: Cross-region is a hard no for PHI.
[10:36] Aisha: Understood. We'll set policy to avoid cross-region fallback for this account.
[10:41] Liam: Anything about monitoring hooks? Event streams for p95 alerts?
[10:46] Marc: Console supports webhooks, Prometheus metrics exporter, and token-level traces.
[10:51] Priya: Great.
[10:53] Aisha: Alright, I'll recap and list actions.
[10:55] Aisha: Actions: 1) Redwood to send benchmark template, pilot pricing, SOC2 attestation. 2) Customer to send infra diagram, HPA metrics, sample prompts. 3) SE to run Dedicated lab microbench and share results. Would you all be comfortable with a follow-up next week?
[11:13] Sofia: Yes.
[11:15] Evan: Works.
[11:16] Priya: Yes.
[11:17] Aisha: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll put notes in the CRM and send the packet.
